strands.name: Introduction to Horticulture and Crop Science

objectives.description: Define horticulture and explain its importance to food production, nutrition, and income in Nigeria
Classify horticultural crops into fruits, vegetables, ornamentals, and herbs with examples from Nigeria
Describe the nutritional and economic value of horticultural crops to Nigerian households and the economy
Identify common farm tools and equipment used in crop production and describe their correct use and maintenance
Describe the composition of soil, soil types (sandy, clay, loam), and their suitability for different crops
Explain methods of improving soil fertility including the use of organic manure, compost, and inorganic fertilisers
Describe land preparation methods including clearing, ploughing, harrowing, and ridging
Explain erosion control and soil conservation practices including mulching, cover cropping, and terracing
Describe methods of crop propagation including seed planting, vegetative propagation, and transplanting seedlings
Apply basic irrigation methods (drip, sprinkler, furrow) and explain their advantages in dry conditions
Identify common pests and diseases affecting Nigerian crops and describe integrated pest management strategies
Apply weeding, mulching, and staking practices to support healthy crop growth
Grow a simple vegetable or herb garden applying correct planting, maintenance, and harvesting techniques
Describe signs of crop maturity and apply appropriate harvesting methods for different horticultural crops
Describe post-harvest handling practices including sorting, grading, packaging, and storage to reduce losses
Identify value-addition opportunities in horticulture including processing, packaging, and marketing of farm produce
Write a simple crop production business plan for a small-scale horticultural enterprise
